blocks.h1: What This Is / What It Is For

blocks.p: The __Message Center__ is where APRS Command collects the text traffic that flows in and out of your station: direct messages addressed to your callsign, club __bulletins__, __announcements__, station __queries__, and the messages you stage to send. It is one window with a row of tabs, plus a compose area along the bottom for building a message to another station.

Open it from the menu bar with **Messages** > **Messages**. The window is titled **APRS Command — Messages** and its panel header reads **Messages**. A short line of guidance sits across the top of the window explaining what the tabs hold.

callout.label: Receiving is always on; sending is not
callout.text: Reading messages, bulletins, announcements, and queries never puts a signal on the air. Composing and sending a message is a **transmit action**. APRS Command ships receive-first with a **TX Disabled** badge in the title bar, and it stays that way until you deliberately enable transmit. Nothing in the Message Center goes out over the air on its own.

blocks.screenshot: The Messages window: tab strip (Inbox, Bulletins, Announcements, Queries, Outbox, Drafts, Thread) filling the upper area, and the bordered compose staging area docked along the bottom with Template, From, To, and Message fields.

blocks.h1: The tabs — what each one holds

blocks.p: The Message Center groups incoming and outgoing traffic into tabs. Click a tab to switch views; the list underneath updates to match.

rows: Direct (private) messages addressed to your callsign — sender, message text, and a timestamp.
General bulletins from other stations, each with the sender, its bulletin ID (for example `BLN0`), the text, and a status.
Announcement-class bulletins, with sender, announcement ID, text, and source.
Incoming APRS station queries (such as `?APRSD`), with the sender, query type, body, and time received.
Messages you have sent or queued to send, with the destination station, the text, and a status.
Messages staged but not yet queued for transmit — destination and text only.
The back-and-forth conversation with one station, showing each message's direction, status, text, and a short validation summary.

blocks.p: Selecting a message in the **Inbox** loads that station's conversation into the **Thread** tab, so you can see the whole exchange in order.

steps: On the **Inbox** tab, click the message you want to read. The row shows the sending station, a preview of the text, and when it arrived.
Switch to the **Thread** tab to see the full exchange with that station — each entry is labeled with its **Direction** (incoming or outgoing) and a **Status**, with the message body wrapped below.
Use the **Bulletins**, **Announcements**, and **Queries** tabs to browse the broader traffic that is not addressed specifically to you.

callout.label: Inbox vs. bulletins
callout.text: The **Inbox** is only messages addressed to your callsign. Club and net bulletins, general announcements, and station queries live on their own tabs so a busy bulletin channel never buries a message meant for you.

blocks.p: The compose area is the bordered panel docked along the bottom of the window — the subtitle under the **Messages** heading calls it __compose staging__. It has four inputs stacked in one row: an optional **Template** picker, **From**, **To**, and **Message**.

bullets: **From** is filled in automatically from your **Station Setup** callsign — you normally leave it alone.
**To** is the destination station's callsign (for example `K8ABC`).
**Message** is the text you want to send.
**Template (optional)** is a dropdown that pre-fills the compose area from your saved templates — see the next section.

blocks.p: A small validation line sits under the fields. It reads **Not validated** until the message is checked, then either **Ready to queue** or a plain-language list of what needs fixing (for example a missing recipient or an over-length body). Fixing the flagged item and re-checking clears the warning.

callout.label: Sending is a transmit action
callout.text: When you send, APRS Command hands the message to its acknowledgement/retry engine: it transmits the message, waits about 30 seconds for an __ACK__ (acknowledgement) from the receiving station, retries up to 3 times if none arrives, and marks the message **Failed** if it still gets no reply. None of this happens while transmit is disabled. Enabling transmit is your decision, made outside this window; until then the app stays receive-only and the **TX Disabled** badge remains in the title bar.

blocks.p: APRS direct messages are confirmed end to end. When the station you messaged receives it, its radio sends back a short __ACK__ packet. APRS Command matches that ACK to your outgoing message and marks it acknowledged right away — you will see the message's **Status** update in the **Outbox** and **Thread** tabs.

bullets: An outgoing message that is transmitted but not yet acknowledged is retried automatically — up to 3 times, roughly 30 seconds apart.
When the ACK arrives, the message is marked acknowledged immediately and retries stop.
If no ACK ever comes back, the message ends up marked **Failed** — a sign the other station did not hear you, or is not on the air.

APRS Command also answers the other direction: when *you* receive a direct message, the acknowledgement handling is part of the same message pipeline (a transmit path that, again, only operates when transmit is enabled).

blocks.p: __Templates__ are canned messages you can drop into the compose area with one pick, so you are not retyping the same check-in or status text every time. They are managed on their own settings tab and used from the Message Center.

steps: In the Message Center, open the **Template (optional)** dropdown above the **From** / **To** / **Message** fields. It is labeled with the placeholder **Pick a template to pre-fill compose…**.
Choose a template. Its name and a preview of its body are shown in the list.
The template fills the **Message** field, and if the template has a default recipient it fills **To** as well. A template with no recipient only fills the body, leaving **To** for you to set.
Edit the pre-filled text if you need to, then send as usual.

callout.label: Pick again freely
callout.text: The dropdown clears its selection after it fills the compose area, so you can pick the same template a second time — handy if you overwrote the text and want the original back.

blocks.p: Templates are managed in **Settings** > **Message Templates** tab. The left side lists your templates; the right side shows the selected template's details or an editor.

steps: Open **Settings** and select the **Message Templates** tab.
Click **+ New Template** at the bottom to start a new one, or select an existing template and click **Edit**.
Fill in **Template name** (required), an optional **Default recipient** callsign, and the **Message body** (required). Leaving the recipient blank means the template only pre-fills the body.
Click **Save**. A status line at the bottom confirms the template was added or updated. Use **Cancel** to back out without saving.
To reorder the list, select a template and use the **↑** (move up) and **↓** (move down) buttons. To remove one, select it and click **Delete**.

blocks.p: APRS Command comes with a set of ready-made templates — for example **Check In** (`Checking in. All OK.`), **At Position**, **Departing**, **Need Assistance**, **All Clear**, **Copy That**, and **Say Again**. If you edit them and want the originals back, click **Restore defaults** at the bottom right of the tab.

callout.label: A template never sends by itself
callout.text: Templates only fill in the compose fields. Choosing one puts text in the box — it does not transmit. Sending is still a separate, deliberate step, and still gated by the transmit setting.

bullets: **A message won't send / nothing goes out.** Transmit is disabled by default — the **TX Disabled** badge in the title bar means the app is receive-only. Enable transmit deliberately before expecting anything on the air.

**The compose line says something other than 'Ready to queue'.** That is the validation summary telling you what is wrong — commonly a missing **To** callsign or a message body that is too long. Fix the flagged item; the line updates when it re-checks.

**A sent message shows as Failed.** No acknowledgement came back after the retries. The other station may be out of range, off the air, or not running an APRS station that ACKs — try again later or via a different path.
**The Template dropdown is empty.** Open **Settings** > **Message Templates** and add one with **+ New Template**, or click **Restore defaults** to bring back the built-in set.
**My From callsign is wrong or blank.** It is pulled from **Station Setup** — set your callsign there and reopen the Message Center.

**A club bulletin isn't in my Inbox.** Bulletins, announcements, and queries are not addressed to you individually — look on the **Bulletins**, **Announcements**, and **Queries** tabs, not the **Inbox**.
**A template I edited doesn't show its recipient.** A blank **Default recipient** is normal — that template only pre-fills the message body and leaves **To** for you to enter.
